findings.quote: „Sophie: „Heute lese ich. Gestern habe ich viel gelacht.“ Was macht Sophie heute?“ · options „Sie lacht viel.“ / „Sie liest.“ / „Sie ist im Museum.“ → „Sie liest.“
findings.problem: Our r2-F02 fix for this item removed the lachen gloss but put the time adverbs into the stimulus. The question's „heute“ now matches „Heute lese ich“, and the key is the only option with that sentence's verb, so a learner who reads neither „lese“ as present nor „habe … gelacht“ as past solves it by matching one word. A Structured-Input item must take the lexical time cue away so that the verb form alone carries the time (the u04 r1-F26 / r2-F03 class: the key is reached without processing the target). The sibling fix ls1-s03 does it right: no adverb in the stimulus, „jetzt“ only in the question. ls1-s02 keeps „Am Sonntag“ and „Heute ist Montag“, but there the learner still has to work out the day, which is LS2's own content, so we do not raise it.
findings.fix: promptDe „Sophie: „Ich habe viel gelacht. Ich lese ein Buch.“ Was macht Sophie jetzt?“ (75 characters), promptEn „What is Sophie doing now?“, options and key unchanged, explanation.de „„Ich lese“ ist jetzt. „habe … gelacht“ ist Perfekt: Das war schon.“ (11 words), en „“Ich lese” is now. “habe … gelacht” is the Perfekt: it already happened.“ Every token is known at a1.1-u11, with no ceiling hit, and it matches the postcard („Heute lese ich nur …“).
findings.proposedRule: ITM-01 advisory, extending r2-F02's proposal: a role 'structured' item whose topic is a tense point (g.perfekt-*, g.praeteritum-*) is reported when one temporal adverb (heute, gestern, vorgestern, jetzt, morgen, letzte Woche, am + weekday) occurs both inside the quoted stimulus and in the question. Failing fixture: a1.1-u11-ls3-s03. Passing fixture: a1.1-u11-ls1-s03. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.quote: statement „Sophie ist am Mittwoch wieder in Leipzig.“ → richtig · t1 „Hallo Sophie, wie geht’s in Dresden? Hier in der WG ist alles gut. … Am Mittwoch kommst du zurück.“ · LS3 postcard „Am Mittwoch bin ich wieder in Leipzig.“ · ls3-i04 „Am ___ ist Sophie wieder in Leipzig.“
findings.problem: The statement names Leipzig, which t1 never mentions. t1 says only that Sophie is in Dresden and comes back („zurück“) to Olena's WG, so the key comes from the story (the WG is in Leipzig), not from the text. The statement is the LS3 postcard sentence in the third person, i.e. ls3-i04 again, so a learner answers it from memory without reading t1. A learner who follows the unit's own strategy card („Dann suchen Sie im Text: Wer? Wann? Was?“) looks for „Leipzig“ in t1, finds only „Dresden“, and may mark falsch. In Start Deutsch 1 Lesen Teil 1 each statement is decided by its text (sd1.json sd1.l1). Here the item trains answering from background knowledge, the behaviour the Teil is built to defeat. The other four statements pass this test. It is the mirror of u04 r2-F06: that finding was a cast text contradicting the story; this is a cast text whose item the story answers. Not a wrong key, since every course learner knows where the WG is, hence MINOR.
findings.fix: Replace the statement with a fact that only t1 carries and that keeps the key richtig (block stays 2 R / 3 F, no run > 3): promptDe „Olena war am Sonntag am See.“, explanation.de „Olena schreibt: „Am Sonntag war ich mit dem Fahrrad am See.““ (en „Olena writes that she rode her bike to the lake on Sunday.“). Both are known at a1.1-u11 with no ceiling hit, and the statement is neither a substring nor a one-token edit of t1 (ITM-04). A weaker minimal edit is „Am Mittwoch ist Sophie wieder in der WG.“ It is decidable from „Hier in der WG“ + „kommst du zurück“, but the story still tells it.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-04 extension: every proper name (cast name, place name) in an R/F or multiple-choice statement of an exam block must occur in the text its textRef names. Failing fixture: a1.1-u11-ls4-sd1-l1-02 („Leipzig“); the other four u11 statements pass. The test runs over all registered courses.
